paragraphs: Rabbi Yirmeyah (a Tanna of a baraita).

Hyman cites Megillah 18a and [Menachot 32b](https://www.sefaria.org/Menachot.32b.4), where a baraita has Rabbi Yirmeyah speaking in the name of “our Rabbi.” He also cites [Horayot 8b](https://www.sefaria.org/Horayot.8b.13), where a baraita introduces what Rabbi Yirmeyah used to say, and traces this to [Tosefta Shevuot 1:4](https://www.sefaria.org/Tosefta_Shevuot.1.4).[^3]
He is also mentioned in the Mekhilta, Bo, chapter 2, and Beshalach, chapter 1, section 7; and in Sifra, Acharei, at locator 143.

notes.text: The Mekhilta locator reads chapter 1, section 7, rather than chapters 1–7. Our teacher is left without a new personal identification.

The parallel for Hyman’s Megillah citation is at [Megillah 18b:16](https://www.sefaria.org/Megillah.18b.16) in the consulted text. Both it and [Menachot 32b:4](https://www.sefaria.org/Menachot.32b.4) say “our Rabbi” in Hebrew. The consulted English identifies that expression as Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi in Megillah and as Rav in Menachot.

The linked Tosefta gives Rabbi Yirmeyah’s argument that the offering discussed in Leviticus applies to someone who can become poor. He excludes the ruler and the anointed high priest. This is the parallel to the teaching cited in Horayot.
